uncited: This family encompasses techniques for rendering volumetric datasets that exceed the memory or processing capacity of a single machine by distributing the workload across multiple nodes or processes.
It solves the scalability bottleneck inherent in single-node rendering by partitioning data or computation.

What sets this family apart from [Out-of-core, streaming and distributed data](8-out-of-core-streaming-and-distributed-data.md) is the explicit focus on simultaneous multi-node processing and load balancing, whereas out-of-core methods primarily address single-node memory limits via disk swapping.

This family inherits the core mechanisms of decomposition, distribution, local rendering, and compositing defined in [Out-of-core, streaming and distributed data](8-out-of-core-streaming-and-distributed-data.md).
Evaluates dataset strings, retrieves world size and rank, and attempts to create a dataset-specific sampler.
If that fails, it falls back to a PyTorch distributed sampler, random sampler, or sequential sampler.
